newsitem.title: USA: Henkel says Loctite bid allowed under rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Henkel says Loctite bid allowed under rights plan.

text.p: German consumer products group Henkel KGaA said on Wednesday its bid for the rest of U.S. adhesives maker Loctite Corp conformed with terms for a "permitted offer" under Loctite's shareholder rights plan.

"It remains our preference to enter into a friendly, negotiated transaction with the management and board of Loctite, and it remains our fervent hope that we will be given the opportunity to do so," Henkel president and chief executive Hans-Dietrich Winkhaus said in a statement.

He added, "To that end we will continue to pursue discussions with the special committee of Loctite's board. However, the special committee has not yet agreed to enter into any discussions or negotiations regarding our proposal."

Henkel's wholly owned subsidiary HC Investments Inc has increased its offer for the 65 percent stake it does not already own in Loctite to $57.75 a share. The offer increase values the whole of Loctite at $1.2 billion.

The statement from the Dusseldorf, Germany-based company said the tender offer was "structured to qualify as a 'permitted offer' under Loctite's stockholder rights plan and as such does not trigger the rights. The tender offer is also conditioned upon HC Investments remaining satisfied that the offer constitutes such a permitted offer."
